title: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification
claim: Standard pipelines yield noisy geometry because one global alignment fits distorted depth; spatially varying rectification gives clean, consistent geometry.
layout: 2 rows, 5 labeled panels; top RGB/mesh comparison, bottom depth maps plus scatter plot
description: The top row shows a reference RGB photo of an indoor room. Next to it is the baseline Splatfacto's rendered RGB with its mesh, which looks noisy and fragmented. Next to that are our rendered RGB and mesh, which looks smooth and clean. The bottom row shows three depth maps in viridis colors: ground-truth disparity, monocular disparity, and a segmentation of the scene into spatial affine regions colored red, gray and orange. A scatter plot titled Local Linear Distortions follows. It plots monocular against ground-truth disparity, with colored line fits per region and an outlier legend, and shows that no single line fits all regions. The last panel is the estimated spatial scale field in an inferno colormap with a colorbar. The eye goes first to the contrast between the noisy and clean meshes, then to the colored regions and the scatter plot.
caption: Robust 3DGS geometry via spatially varying affine rectification. (a-c) Standard 3DGS overfits appearance, producing noisy underlying geometry. In contrast, our method extracts clean, highly accurate meshes while maintaining photorealism. (d) Monocular disparity exhibits piecewise-linear distortions, proving that a single global scale-and-shift alignment is fundamentally insufficient (scatter plot). (e) We overcome this by estimating an edge-aware spatial scale field (αsmooth) to rectify the monocular depth prior, yielding geometrically consistent 3D representations.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become the leading approach for photorealistic novel view synthesis, yet its geometric accuracy lags behind its visual quality. Existing depth-guided methods attempt to resolve this by regularizing the optimization with monocular depth priors, typically using a single global scale-and-shift alignment. Crucially, we discover a fundamental flaw in this assumption: modern monocular depth networks systematically exhibit region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions. This discovery invalidates standard global alignment strategies, which warp scene geometry by enforcing a single transform. To address this, we introduce a spatially varying affine rectification model that corrects monocular disparity into consistent metric depth using regionally smooth, edge-aware fields. We further derive a normal-aware regularizer that uses spatial gradients to couple the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. Across diverse experimental settings, our sensor-free method shows strong photometric quality of Gaussian Splatting while substantially improving geometric accuracy and outperforming state-of-the art geometry-focused methods.
